header.sector: Power generation, grid and interconnection for AI datacenters
header.title: Rates, data-center moratoriums pressure utilities despite AI power demand

s01_bottom_line.text: S&P 500 Utilities swung from a July peak above 10% to about -10% since May as state data-center moratoriums (New York, then Texas restrictions in early August) and rising bond yields weighed on the dividend-valued sector. ⟨cited figures: approximate, read from a chart; data as of 2026-09-30⟩
The article frames utilities as a microcosm of the AI promise, political backlash and higher-rate reality, illustrating how sectors respond differently to the same macro forces.
The article presents utilities as hurt by policy moratoriums on data-center build-out and by higher yields competing with their dividends, but does not quantify the earnings impact.

items.text: S&P 500 Utilities peaked above 10% price return in July then fell to around -10% by end September (since May). ⟨cited figures: approximate, read from a chart; data as of 2026-09-30⟩
